modelName: Sorting the social determinants — public, commons, private
modelNote: Which determinants MUST be public goods, which MUST be local commons, and which are private. The sort is not a judgement call: it falls out of rivalry (does my use diminish yours) and excludability (can anyone be kept out). Each cell then has a level, a verifier and a funding source — and they line up with Marc's own three levels, Individual / Group / EIP. Every node carries a hover note with the reasoning. Drawn Aug 16 2026.

legendEntries.label: PUBLIC GOOD — EIP level · governed · tax-funded · never an order
COMMONS — Group level · NDC · place orders and capacity
PRIVATE GOOD — Individual level · person orders · the dān
CLUB GOOD — the co-op's own instruments
The test that makes it a MUST

nodes.label: SPLIT THE DETERMINANT FIRST. Housing is not one good: the unit is private, the codes are public, the block is commons. Assign the bundle whole and you get it wrong three ways at once.
nodes.note: This is the move that makes the whole frame work. Almost no social determinant is a single good — each is a bundle whose pieces sit in different cells and therefore need different money, different verifiers and different governance. Sort the pieces, never the headline.

nodes.label: NON-EXCLUDABLE — nobody can be kept out
nodes.note: The left half of the frame. Where you cannot exclude, you cannot sell, so the market will not provide it and something else must.

nodes.label: EXCLUDABLE — access can be limited
nodes.note: The right half. Excludability is what makes a price possible, which is what makes a contract possible — which is why the person register works here and nowhere else.

nodes.label: NON-RIVAL
nodes.note: My use does not diminish yours. Herd immunity, clean air, a broadcast, a standard. Once it exists, one more beneficiary costs nothing.

nodes.label: RIVAL
nodes.note: My use DOES diminish yours. This is the axis people skip, and it is the one that separates a public good from a commons. A commons can be exhausted; a public good cannot.

nodes.label:
PUBLIC GOODS
EIP level · governed · tax-funded
never an order
nodes.note: Non-rival and non-excludable. Free-riding guarantees that voluntary local provision fails, which is exactly why these need a public purse and a governing body rather than a contract. In the workbench they appear as standing capacity with no gate — the same shape as public health surveillance.

nodes.label:
CLUB GOODS
The co-op's own instruments
nodes.note: Non-rival but excludable: one more member costs nearly nothing, and membership can be limited. These are not determinants of health — they are the machinery the co-op uses to buy the things that are.

nodes.label:
COMMON-POOL / COMMONS
Group level · NDC · place orders
plus unconditional capacity
nodes.note: Rival but non-excludable — the hardest cell, and the one health care has no vocabulary for. Ostrom's finding is that these are governed well by neither market nor state alone: they need collective-choice arrangements made by the people who use them. That is the Group level of your own frame, and it is why the NDC is a production site rather than a service window.

nodes.label:
PRIVATE GOODS
Individual level · person orders
the dān
nodes.note: Rival and excludable. This is the only cell where a named person can be the counterparty and their own verification can release payment — which is precisely why the medical register works and why it cannot be stretched to cover the left-hand side of this frame.

nodes.label: Air and water QUALITY
nodes.note: The textbook public good. Note the split from quantity: an aquifer is RIVAL and therefore a commons. Same substance, two entirely different governance problems, and confusing them is how water fights start.

nodes.label: Communicable disease control and surveillance
nodes.note: Scale exceeds any group, success is a non-event, and it must exist before anyone knows what for. Three separate reasons it can never be an order.

nodes.label: Habitability codes and enforcement
nodes.note: Adversarial. The inspected party can never be the verifier, which rules out the whole verification mechanism and puts this permanently in public hands.

nodes.label: Street network, sidewalks, lighting
nodes.note: The built network itself is non-rival at normal use. Its CAPACITY at peak is rival, which is why the same street appears in the commons cell below.

nodes.label: Emergency response
nodes.note: Failure is catastrophic and irreversible, so it cannot ride on local capacity that varies block to block.

nodes.label: Universal schooling as a system
nodes.note: The system is public; the school as a neighbourhood institution is a commons; a particular credential is private. Another bundle needing the splitting rule.

nodes.label: Co-op membership
nodes.note: Excludable by membership, non-rival in use. The club good is the co-op's standing, not a determinant of anyone's health.

nodes.label: The workbench itself
nodes.note: The order register, contracts, ledger and verification machinery. One more member costs almost nothing to serve, which is what makes a co-op the right owner of it.

nodes.label: This cell holds instruments, not determinants — worth knowing so nobody looks for health outcomes in it.
nodes.note: Kept on the drawing because an empty quadrant makes people assume something is missing. Nothing is missing; the cell is simply not where health comes from.

nodes.label: The food ENVIRONMENT
nodes.note: What is within walking distance. Non-excludable and rival — a shelf empties, a shop closes. The food itself is private and sits in the opposite cell.

nodes.label: CHW time and appointment capacity
nodes.note: A commons hiding inside a private-good billing system. It is rival — my slot is not yours — and currently rationed by queue rather than governed. Naming it as a commons is what lets it be scheduled by agreement instead of by whoever calls first.

nodes.label: Eyes on the street — informal safety
nodes.note: Jacobs. Rival in attention, non-excludable in benefit, and co-produced by the people who live there. Police cannot manufacture it; it is the thing that prevents most harm and appears in no budget.

nodes.label: Neighbourhood condition and tenure stability
nodes.note: Displacement is zero-sum, which makes stability rival. This is the piece of 'housing' that is neither the unit nor the code, and it is the piece most place orders will be about.

nodes.label: Road and transit CAPACITY at peak
nodes.note: The same street that is a public good at 10am is a commons at 5pm. Congestion is what turns a public good into a common-pool resource, which is why capacity is governed differently from construction.

nodes.label: Aquifer and groundwater
nodes.note: Ostrom's own case. Rival and non-excludable, exhaustible, and successfully governed for generations by the users themselves in places where the state failed and the market failed.

nodes.label: BELONGING AND MUTUAL AID
nodes.note: The proof case for 'must'. Your own frame has Group Size -> Belonging as a NEGATIVE link, which means belonging has a size ceiling in its production function. It is therefore the one social determinant of health that is provably undeliverable at state scale. A government can fund the conditions for it and can never produce it. This is the strongest argument in the whole frame for why NDCs are structurally necessary rather than merely nice.

nodes.label: KNOWLEDGE AND SKILL — SODOTO
nodes.note: Anti-rival: it GROWS with use. See one, do one, teach one increases the stock by being consumed. Enclose it behind a price and the mechanism that made it valuable stops working. Anti-rival goods are the clearest 'must' of all, because privatising them is not merely unfair, it is self-defeating.

nodes.label: The dwelling unit
nodes.note: Rival and excludable — genuinely private. Making it affordable is redistribution, which is a different instrument from changing a good's type. Subsidy does not make housing a commons.

nodes.label: Groceries and meals
nodes.note: Private. The food ENVIRONMENT that determines what is available to buy is not.

nodes.label: Medications
nodes.note: Private and contractable — which is why a pharmacy ME can hold part of a person order.

nodes.label: A specific clinical service
nodes.note: The core of the medical register. Named person, excludable service, verifiable by the person who received it.

nodes.label: Income and cash transfer
nodes.note: Cash is rival and excludable. Income support is a transfer, not a public good — worth being precise about, because calling it a public good invites the wrong governance.

nodes.label:
MUST be PUBLIC if any one holds:
non-rival AND non-excludable · adversarial or regulatory · scale exceeds any possible group · failure catastrophic and irreversible
nodes.note: Any single one of these is sufficient. The adversarial test is the one most often missed, and it is decisive: wherever the party being checked would be the verifier, the whole verification mechanism has to be replaced by public authority.

nodes.label: TEST 1 · ANTI-RIVAL — it grows with use, and enclosing it destroys it
nodes.note: Knowledge, skill, trust, norms, reputation, language. Privatising an anti-rival good is self-defeating rather than merely unjust, because the value came from the sharing.

nodes.label: TEST 2 · SIZE CEILING — its production function cannot scale
nodes.note: Group Size -> Belonging is negative in your frame. A good whose production falls as the group grows cannot be produced by a large body at all, at any budget. Federation is the only route upward — you do not grow the group, you federate groups.

nodes.label: TEST 3 · CO-PRODUCED — the beneficiaries are the producers
nodes.note: Ostrom's co-production. Mutual aid, informal care, watchfulness, a functioning street. These cannot be delivered to passive recipients, which is why a service window cannot produce them and a group can.

nodes.label: ERROR 1 · ENCLOSURE — selling what only worked shared
nodes.note: Moving a commons into the right-hand column. Familiar, well documented, and usually visible while it happens.

nodes.label: ERROR 2 · CROWDING OUT — paying for acts of neighbourliness
nodes.note: The live risk in the WWHA design. If a third of the savings reaches NDCs and NDCs begin paying neighbours per act of care, the reciprocity norm is replaced by a transaction that is worse and costs more than what it displaced. The design rule that follows: FUND CAPACITY AND CONDITIONS, NEVER ACTS. Pay for the convening, the crew, the tools, the crossing. Never per check-in on a neighbour.

edges.label: quality is public, quantity is a commons
the network is public, its capacity is a commons
the block is commons, the unit is private
the environment is commons, the food is private
